dish.title: Greek Avgolemono Chicken Soup with Rice, Lemon, and Dill
dish.description: Chicken thighs simmered in chicken broth with onion, carrot, celery, and bay, then shredded back into the pot with long-grain rice and thickened with a tempered mixture of eggs and lemon juice into a silky soup finished with dill.

recipe_version.title: Greek Avgolemono Chicken Soup with Rice, Lemon, and Dill
recipe_version.description: Chicken thighs simmered in chicken broth with onion, carrot, celery, and bay, then shredded back into the pot with long-grain rice and thickened with a tempered mixture of eggs and lemon juice into a silky soup finished with dill.

ingredients.name: chicken broth
ingredients.display_name: low-sodium chicken broth whose label lists chicken stock, salt, and vegetable flavorings

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Dice the onion, carrots, and celery. Juice the lemons and chop the dill.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.body: Put the broth, chicken, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaves, and salt in the covered 5.5-quart Dutch oven and bring to a boil over medium-high, about 10 minutes to come to a boil. Simmer gently until the chicken reaches 175 F, about 15 minutes. Lift out the chicken and shred it with 2 forks.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: Stir the rice into the simmering broth and cook uncovered until tender, about 15 minutes. Discard the bay leaves and return the chicken. Turn the heat to low.

steps.title: Temper the egg-lemon
steps.body: Whisk the eggs in the medium bowl until frothy, then whisk in the lemon juice. Whisking constantly, ladle in 2 cups of the hot broth, one ladleful at a time.

steps.title: Thicken and serve
steps.body: Stir the egg-lemon into the pot over low and stir until the soup thickens slightly and reaches 160 F, about 3 minutes; do not boil. Season with pepper, scatter dill over each bowl, and serve.

coverage_contribution: The catalog has no chicken soup apart from pho and ajiaco, and no Greek soup. An everyday weeknight poultry soup.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with colombian-ajiaco: a lemon-egg thickened rice soup, not a potato and corn soup with capers and cream. Compared with vietnamese-chicken-pho: a silky lemon-egg broth with rice, not a spiced clear broth with rice noodles. Compared with spanish-sopa-de-ajo-egg: chicken and rice thickened with tempered egg and lemon, not a garlic bread soup with poached eggs.
not_duplicate_of: Not plain chicken rice soup (the egg-lemon makes it), and not Greek lemon potatoes.
